chunks: Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh ibn Nusayr, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj and others – he said: Zurara sent his son Ubayd to Medina to inquire about the matter of Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) and Abdallah ibn Abi Abdillah, but he (Zurara) died before Ubayd could return to him … I said to Abu al-Hasan the first (peace be upon him) and mentioned to him Zurara and his sending his son Ubayd to Medina, so Abu al-Hasan said: I do hope that Zurara is among those about whom Allah the Exalted said:
And whoever comes out of his home emigrating to Allah and His Messenger – and death overtakes him – then he has already secured his reward from Allah.

key_terms.أَبِي الْحَسَنِ الْأَوَّلِ: Abu al-Hasan al-Kadhim, the seventh Imam
key_terms.زُرَارَة: Zurara, a prominent companion of the Imams

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Zurara's death before receiving news about the Imam in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This narrative from Rijal al-Kashshi recounts how the companion Zurara sent his son Ubayd to Medina to verify the status of Imam al-Kadhim (Abu al-Hasan) and his brother Abdallah, but Zurara died before receiving the news. Imam al-Kadhim expressed hope that Zurara would be rewarded as a migrant (muhajir) based on the Quranic verse (4:100), linking his act of sending his son for knowledge/verification to the spiritual status of emigration. In Shia exegesis, this highlights the concept of 'muhajirun' extending beyond physical migration to include those who journey for religious verification and knowledge, emphasizing the merit of the companion's intent and the Imam's endorsement of his scholarly pursuit.
